utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Mr. Bakrac, your next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Radojko Stefanovic is our next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stefanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated. You will now be examined by Mr. Bakrac on behalf of Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stefanovic, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to introduce yourself so that we have this in the transcript, your name and surname.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Radojko Stefanovic, born on the 31st of July, 1954, Pozega, Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, I would just like to ask you to wait a second so that my question is interpreted, so that we don't have any overlap between the question and the answer and so that we avoid mistakes in the transcript. Mr. Stefanovic, tell us, what is your education?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: After I completed secondary school, general high school, I entered the military academy of the land forces and graduated from that academy. I graduated from all the existing schools in the Army of Yugoslavia up to the top ones, including the staff college.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a pensioner; to be very precise, I have been one since 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You retired with what rank?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what were all the military positions that you held during your career?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: During my military career, I started out as platoon leader up to the Chief of Staff of the army, so from the very lowest to the very highest. Over the 28 years of my career, I spent 25 years in commanding positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What were your duties in 1998??

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 I was commander of the mixed artillery brigade in the Gnjilane garrison.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Until when?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: I held that position until the 20th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Where were you transferred on the 20th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of January, 1999, I reported to the command of the Pristina Corps in order to assume the duty the chief of the organ for operations and training.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you start carrying out those duties immediately on the 20th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, because when an officer assumes a particular post, then a certain time is required for him to take over that duty properly; then a plan of duty handover is elaborated, according to which the duty is taken over.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: From who was it that you took over this duty and when did you, in fact, take over?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: As for this duty, chief of organ for operations and training, that is a duty that I received from General Djakovic, it was about a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Tesevic, what was his duty? What was his post?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Tesevic was chief of the sector for operations in the organ for operations and training. At the same time he was the deputy chief of organ. He was Djakovic's deputy. After Djakovic was transferred to another duty to the army command, he stayed on as my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please be so kind as to explain to us briefly what your line of work was when you assumed this duty?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: This organ in the corps command has the following duties: It is of a planning and operations nature and it has to do with training, combat training, in peacetime and in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During the handover of duty and when you were taking over this duty, can you tell us what the intelligence and security position of the Pristina Corps was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The Pristina Corps in this period of time had the following intelligence and security operations position. The aggression was becoming ever-more imminent. There was a build-up of troops in the Republic of Macedonia and Albania, there were numerous problems every day at the state border. There was an escalation of terrorist forces throughout Kosovo and Metohija, and according to their own statements they were preparing for a spring offensive. Furthermore, the corps had insufficient forces for carrying out normal, regular, everyday duties. Because in that period of time the corps was manned at an 80 per cent level in terms of all structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "manned 80 per cent in terms of all structures," are you referring to peacetime or wartime establishment?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: I meant peacetime establishment. Furthermore, the operations and mobilisation development hadn't even started and, ultimately, the operative position of the Pristina Corps was highly unfavourable.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please be so kind as to explain to us briefly what the method of work of the command of the Pristina Corps was in peacetime and in wartime in terms of making decisions for the engagement of forces of the corps in carrying out combat activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The corps command, as the operative command, had an elaborated methodology of its work on a daily, weekly, monthly [Realtime transcript read in error missing word "monthly"], and periodical basis. The corps commander organized meetings of his collegium every week, once every seven days. At these collegium meetings, all questions were discussed that pertained to the functioning of the military organization. After that, specific tasks were assigned for the corps command and for subordinate units. During the course of the war, the work of the corps command evolved in a planned and organized manner on the basis of existing instructions and rules. In order for the corps command to work properly, it has to be given an assignment, a task; that is to say that an assigned task is the very basis. The method of work can be a complete method, an abbreviated method, a team-based method, and with consultations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: And the stages, the stages in the method of work consist of three stages: Assessing the situation, or rather, analysing it; analysing the decision that is to be made; and planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, may I stop you at this point. We are going to deal with this specifically, how the Pristina Corps functioned at the relevant point in time. I just have an intervention in line 5 on page 4, "monthly" is missing, monthly report.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Monthly reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: There is daily, weekly, and there is supposed to be monthly and periodical. "Periodical" is already there. So, General, tell us specifically as far as the Pristina Corps is concerned, once a task is received what happens then?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: When the corps command receives a task, an assignment, the commander brings together the organs of the command, then the task is studied in order to enhance its comprehension. The basic idea is conceived by the commander. This basic idea is submitted to the superior commander - in this case the army commander. When we're talking about the corps commander, then his superior is the army commander. After the basic idea is approved by the superior commander - in this case the army commander, the commander of the 3rd Army - what happens is the assessment of the situation, submitting proposals to the organ of the command. After that, the commander makes a decision and tells the corps command organs about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let me stop you at this point, General. You were saying the corps commander receives a task, from who?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: From the commander of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just give us a moment, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, we are concerned about the extent to which at this point we should be hearing evidence that's repeating what we've heard on more than one occasion before. This is very theoretical evidence at the moment. We really want to know what was actually happening in particular circumstances. You've already had the evidence of the commander himself and you've had evidence from a number of senior generals throughout the case. So please try to concentrate on the issues that are the important issues in dispute between us, bearing in mind that we're already into overtime so far as the presentation of your case is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I was about to move on to specific documents or the drafting of documents. Just another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you think -- you think we don't know enough about the drafting of documents already? If that's your view, then you have to lead this evidence; but I am somewhat surprised that we've got nearly two years into the case and you don't think we know enough about the drafting of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wasn't saying you don't know enough about it. I was to move on to specific documents. This was just an introduction that I make to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, when you say a task from the 3rd Army command, can a corps commander receive a task from anyone else?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: A corps commander can only receive a task from his superior commander; in this situation it would have been the 3rd Army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, we've seen that, we're not going into theory anymore. When a task is received, when one starts drafting combat documents, who is it that actually drafts them and what are these combat documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Combat documents are orders, decisions, and plans, a decision by the corps commander, an order by the corps commander, plans, orders by assistant corps commanders, and all the various organs and branches in a corps command. All these documents make up an action plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are all these documents produced at the same time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: If the circumstances are as good as can be, the tendency is to draft all these documents at the same time. However, since the corps command was facing highly complex circumstances, the first thing that was done was the basic documents, in this case a combat order, orders that were put in writing and delivered to subordinate commands. As to the decision, it simply took more time to make, for a draftsman who was in charge to do it properly according to the rules, to create all the excerpts that were then delivered to subordinate commands, and finally to deliver these to subordinate commands. If you allow, before all of this, a decision must be ratified by the commander, before these excerpts are produced, a corps command or, if that is the appropriate level, an army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let's move on to more hands-on examples.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 5D1169.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to come up, sir, you talked about the operative situation of the Pristina Corps at the time you took up your duties there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is an order by the 3rd Army command dated the 27th of January, 1999, on the use of the 3rd Army to prevent a NATO brigade being brought in by force in order to crush and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is one we have no translation and it is not a short one that we could probably try to plough through without one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just check. I think there actually is a translation because we have used this document already. Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is both a 3D and a 4D number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the 3D number, Mr. Visnjic? Is it possible, Mr. Bakrac, to move on and come back to this document once you've had some assistance in finding the English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document is related to the following documents that we're about to show this witness, about the actions. So if I can please appeal to your patience because we are trying to show that it is based on this action that some action order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's an appeal to the non-existent, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- some action orders headed "the Joint Command" will result. 4D332. There is a translation, and I think there's one for 5D as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we should be looking at 4D332, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's a command [as interpreted] produced by the 3rd Army command. As you said a while ago, this was an order on the use of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we please go to the last paragraph of page 1 and the first paragraph of page 2. And can you please explain what this document envisages, this order in fact?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you just take me through it one by one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The last paragraph of page 1 which then spills over into paragraph 1 on page 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the first paragraph of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what we see here is a description of the concentration or build-up of terrorist forces in Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo areas?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, those were the three areas at the time where the terrorist forces were at their most concentrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to item 4: "I hereby decide ..." There is a decision there. This is page 5 of the B/C/S -- page 4, rather, of the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's look at the actual decision that the 3rd Army takes here, it's the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed. Shall I read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Further, carry out mobilisation of the army and in cooperation with forces from the air force and anti-aircraft defence and the interior ministry of the Republic of Serbia, prevent the engagement of sabotage and terrorist forces" -- or rather, "working with the interior ministry forces block sabotage and terrorist forces and prevent them from linking to or cooperating with the NATO Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we please go to page 6 of the Serbian, and please explain what that means. It reads: "Armed [Realtime transcript read in error "unarmed"] non-Siptar population is to be engaged on securing military facilities and roads and in order to defend unsettled areas with non-Siptar population ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is, in fact, the armed non-Siptar population or in this instance is it the unarmed, as quoted in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Armed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What does this particular clause mean within the framework of this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of this order, this means that these are forces from the Federal Ministry of Defence engaged in tasks of civilian defence and protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment now. General, who actually writes out the original draft of this document? Is it someone in the 3rd Army or is it someone in the Pristina Corps who drafts it for approval by the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I understand your question if we're talking about this specific document, this order on the use of the 3rd Army was produced by the 3rd Army command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Going back to your answer in relation to armed non-Siptar population, which you say were forces from the Federal Ministry of Defence, why did the forces of the Federal Ministry of Defence exclude Siptars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was in no position to know why the use of the Federal Ministry of Defence was defined in the way set out here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're being presented to us as the man who really knows the organization -- the organizational structure of the forces. So where will we get the answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the only place you could get a proper answer for this is the Federal Ministry of Defence, from the actual people who decided on this definition, because this is something that was simply used in its entirety from elsewhere. It wasn't us who decided on this type of engagement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So someone must have told you to use that expression?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, Your Honour. If we look at this order we see the clause here, and in all the orders drafted by the Pristina Corps command we applied the same clause throughout. This is a task that cannot be changed, amended, or simply left out; it is simply something that you take from the superior command in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Speaking as just an ordinary layperson, it does on the face of it look ridiculous to describe Ministry of Defence forces as the armed non-Siptar population; however, let's move on. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, did you get those forces involved? You say that you applied the clause from the order. Did they see any practical involvement in any of the actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Defined like this, in no order of the Pristina Corps commander were these forces considered and they were never involved, and the best way to see this is if we go to item 4 of the corps commander's decision and also if we go to item 5 which details tasks for units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: For these forces to see any involvement at all on a specific mission, was there something that needed doing first?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In order for these forces to see any practical involvement, first they would have had to be resubordinated. This was a precondition for any involvement on their part by the corps commander, which never materialised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please go to 5D249 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you do. Does that mean that the instruction - and it's in English in the middle of the page we're looking at - which says: "Engage the armed non-Siptar population," is meaningless?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I don't think I fully understand your question, Your Honour. What exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've just told us that for any specific task to be given to the armed non-Siptar population, they would have to be resubordinated. Now, in this document in English the short paragraph after the very long one, it may not be -- or it may be the -- about the seventh line or so in the B/C/S -- in fact, that's where it is. The first full paragraph on that page it says in English, and hopefully the meaning's identical in Serb: "Engage the armed non-Siptar population," now that seems to be an order, but does that mean that it's meaningless; it has absolutely no meaning or effect in this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, here it is formally noted to that effect, but the command -- the corps command was not duty-bound to implement that because it was not able to implement that because these were not its forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, why on earth would the 3rd Army then give you that order, knowing that it can't be implemented? And it's not the first example we've come across of this. The documents of the VJ are riddled with these.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, probably the 3rd Army command had its reasons for formulating it like that, and at this point I'm really unable to comment on that. The only thing was that I said that these were organized forces of the federal organs, the civilian protection and the civilian defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we look at 5D249, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, this is also a document of the 3rd Army command of the 1st of February. Can you please briefly with me look at the second page of the B/C/S and the tasks under the heading "order," tasks under 4 and 5. These paragraphs 4 and 5, can we see that the Pristina Corps was given an assignment to draft a plan by February 15th to block and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo sectors?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is in paragraph 5, which states that the corps command should draft a plan for blocking and destroying the forces in these mentioned sectors, Drenica, Lab, and Malisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. -- Sir, can you tell us another name for the Lab sector? Is there a different name for it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In the geographical sense, that area has several names, Lab, Malo Kosovo, Podujevo. The most acceptable name is Malo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P2808.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This is an order of the Pristina Corps command, it seems, of the 16th of February, 1999, and it refers to the following: "Order to break up and destroy the STS in the Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo sector." Is this an order pursuant to a previous order of the 1st of February to do this assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was the 3rd Corps [as interpreted] command order pursuant to an order by the army commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's a mistake in the transcript on line 25 it says order of the commander of the 3rd Corps but actually it should state the order of the commander of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, in order to cover our ground more quickly, did you have the opportunity to see this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, not only did I see it, I actually drafted it with my team of associates.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: These initials, S.R., are these your initials?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, since you drafted this document and you had the opportunity to see it while it was being prepared, this document specifically, the order of the Pristina Corps to break up the terrorist forces, was there any specific assignment given to the formation of non-armed Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was not given. Like I said previously, we can look at item 4 and item 5, and we can see in the tasks issued to the units there is no such clause.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If it does appear, you may be sure that my learned friend Mr. Stamp will react to that, but we need to move on. Can you please tell me this: Paragraph 2, corps tasks, the same clause is there, formulated in exactly the same way as in the document that we saw before, the order of the 3rd Army. This article -- paragraph 2, tasks to the Pristina Corps, is this something that can be changed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is an assignment issued by the superior commander to the subordinate command, and it is being assumed in its entirety without adding, including, or excluding anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We haven't seen the 3rd Army order here, have we?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, we have the order of the 3rd Army is actually the first document that we looked at in relation to which Mr. Stamp reacted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- stating that it didn't have any translation, this is 5D1169.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I am just interested in your comments on another paragraph from this document and then we can move on, please. Page 5, page 5, first paragraph, "Readiness." Can you briefly comment on the meaning of "readiness" and when was the dead-line for this order to be executed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In this command "readiness" was defined in the follow way: "For increased and in-depth security of the state border, preventing the infiltration of Siptar terrorist forces, for closing off axes from the Republic of Albania and the Republic of Macedonia, and for securing facilities and roads immediately." And, second: "For breaking up and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija after the Munja signal on D plus three to four days."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you please explain what that means.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: That means that the planning documents for all the branches are planned including the signal which is here mentioned as Munja. So you wait for the signal and then embark on the execution of the given actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now look at Exhibit 6D1416.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, are you familiar with this document and can you please briefly tell us what it means and to which sectors does it refer?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the Pristina Corps command. The idea is to carry out an action to break up the Siptar forces in the Severni Drenica and -- in the northern Drenica and Podujevo sectors. And this is a corps document given to the commander of the 3rd Army for approval and verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at Exhibit 5D273.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We saw that the previous document bore the date of the 18th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm advised, Mr. Bakrac, that 5D273 does not exist in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's an error in the system and my associate will try to see -- well, the document has two paragraphs. If you permit me, we can place the document on the ELMO --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the General can look at it and read it. It's a very short document, and then later we will see what the error in the system is exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, we have never had a copy of this document. It does present us with a lot of difficulties proceeding in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is odd is that it has such a low number but does not appear to have been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, an error simply is possible, an error that it was given a number but it was not placed in the system or disclosed. Otherwise there is no other reason. It's a very short document and it's an approval to this -- of this idea, so it's just this -- a kind of technical document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I doubt if it's going to cause prejudice, Mr. Stamp. If it does, then you'll have the benefit of any remedy that's necessary to secure justice. So let's proceed using the ELMO. You'll need to get the witness to read the part that matters, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, you would agree, well, let's just move quickly, that this is a document of the 3rd Corps command of the 19th of March, 1999, sent to the command of the Pristina Corps, to the commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And now can you please read the reference and the first two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Reference: Your act strictly confidential number 455-43 of the 18th of March, 1999." First paragraph: "I approve the idea of executing an action for breaking up Siptar terrorist forces in the region -- sectors of northern Drenica and Podujevo on the 20th and 21st of March, 1999." Second paragraph: "The planned manner of action and engagement of planned forces of the corps with reinforcements in coordination with the forces of MUP is how you will implement or execute the set objective of the action."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this idea for the 20th and the 21st of March, for the action, was it actually implemented?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: From what I can recall, this action was partially executed. Not all the forces were ready for the execution of this action, except for the 37th Combat Group, or rather, BG-37, which was attacked and was, therefore, forced to defend itself from an attack of the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, sir. Was there another idea drafted immediately after that for an action?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 5D276 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, this is an idea from the 22nd of March for the Donja Drenica and Gornji Lab sectors. The time of execution is planned, this is the 23rd to the 25th of March, 1999. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is also an idea for an action to be executed in the fight against terrorist forces. Also, the corps commander sent it to the army commander for the verification of this idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the English version states "plan," but actually it's an idea. So in the original it's stated "zamisao," idea, for carrying out or executing an action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, now we're going to look at the next document and that is a document P1966 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before you move on if we could have that back just briefly. The translation issue that you're raising, the second paragraph in English starts: "The concrete plan for carrying out the operation is as follows ..." Now, in English you would never talk about a concrete idea. To be concrete it would have to be a plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in the Serbian version it says "konkreta zamisao," so for carrying out an action. It becomes a plan once it is approved by the higher command, by the command of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, if that's the technical distinction, that's a different matter. Thank you. We can move to the next one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could we please look at document P1966 now, and you are going to tell me, this has to do with destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Malo Kosovo. The previous idea and the previous approvals, do they pertain to this particular action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, however, it said "Podujevo" over there in the idea, whereas here it says "Malo Kosovo," lest there be any confusion. I talked about that a while ago as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, first of all tell me, whose decision is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a decision of the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the heading why does it say "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you for a bit more time because I need a bit more time to explain this. During the handover of my duty at the corps command I was then told by General Djakovic, who was handing the duty over to me, that the combat document entitled "zapovest," order, is formulated for actions that are carried out by the army and the MUP, and the heading says "Joint Command." And instead of the commander's signature, where the signature should be it says "Joint Command" as well, and also there is this clause that all forces would be commanded by the Joint Command. There are two forms there, two forms of these documents, that is, one where in the heading and in the signature it is the command of the Pristina Corps, rather, the commander with this clause of commanding the forces and then -- that was more seldom. And then this other one, the one that we see now on our screens, that was more frequently present. In the heading it would say "Joint Command," and at the place where the signature of the commander is supposed to be it also says "Joint Command." And when it says command, all forces will be commanded by the Joint Command. This was taken over from 1998 and it was only for situations where forces of the army and forces of the MUP were engaged in the struggle against terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was this form kept somewhere or did you re-type these documents every time at the operations organ?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The form of this order was in the computer and it stayed on in 1999, the beginning of 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you explain a little more about the circumstances in which the other form was used, where in the heading and the signature it is the commander of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, to the best of my recollection and during the handover of duty when reviewing the documentation involved, this has to do with 1998 primarily, it is characteristic of that period. As for 1999, from the time when I took over this duty, this other form of dealing with documents was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us look at paragraph 11 of this same document, it is page 4 in B/C/S. "Command and communications" is the heading, KM, that's what it says in the first sentence, the command post of the Pristina command -- of the Pristina Corps in peacetime. Can you explain this decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a formality that was carried out on purpose, simply to protect the secrecy of the deployment of command posts; or in soldierly terms, this is operative camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us move on to the next page, the last page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that -- sorry. This doesn't actually tell me anything. I may be alone in that. This command post could be identified, but are you saying that in fact it wasn't the peacetime command post that was being used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Exactly. Exactly, Mr. President. That's the way it was written. The command building is intact to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But it was not being used as the command post at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The bombing started on the 24th of March, in the evening. Most of the command wasn't there, and from the 25th onwards there was no one left in that building except for the necessary security of the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, please look at the last page, paragraph 13. It seems that yet again there is a reference to command. Could you please look at both paragraphs and give us your comments. Why is paragraph 13 there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 13 defines "coordinated action with MUP forces concerning preparations for combat operations before the start and during the actual implementation of actions." This last paragraph: "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija shall command and direct all forces during combat operations from the Pristina area." "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija shall command and direct all forces during combat operations from the Pristina area." And finally it says: "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." As I've already said, this is a document, a combat order, of the commander of the Pristina Corps. This clause is here and it can be explained as follows. Since we have different forces, different structures, of the army and of the police and our rules envisage in case such different structures are engaged, a combined command post from which everyone autonomously commands his own forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stefanovic, from the point of view of theory, is there any reason at all why this order would be any less effective if instead of "the Joint Command" it simply said "Pristina Corps command" and was signed by the Pristina Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, there is an immense difference. In command it is clearly defined there is only one person that commands, that is, the commander, not some joint body that is established or can be established. There is an immense difference involved. In command it is clearly defined, there is only one person who is in command, and that is the commander. That is the quality of command as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean you never see in -- well, let me start that question again. Just look at the sentence, the last sentence of this order before the signature by the Joint Command. Would you ever see in a document of this nature: The Pristina Corps commander will command and direct all forces during combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask you to repeat your question because I did not understand the first part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In a document of this nature, an order, does it ever -- or does such a document ever contain the statement: The commander of the Pristina Corps shall command and direct all forces during combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, there is the possibility of defining it that way, but this is what is required beforehand, that all forces in the area where combat operations are being carried out should be resubordinated to the commander of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I'll go back now to my original question which you pointed out I phrased badly. If this document made it clear that the commander was the Pristina Corps commander rather than the Joint Command, would it be any less effective as an order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, we are talking about a specific order here, and it is very difficult now at this point in time to assess -- however, at any rate, I repeat, and all combat rules and instructions define that, that only one person is in command and that is the commander. By no means is it a body, regardless of what it's called. There is no Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're not really answering my question directly. I'm trying to understand whether this order, according to you, would mean the same if the word "Joint Command" was replaced by "commander of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, a few minutes ago that is what I said to you. Only in a situation when all the forces in the area of combat operations were to be subordinated to the corps command, then the corps commander would indeed have that right of command and to carry out these tasks that had been set.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we come full circle. What on earth is this Joint Command that is, according to this document, to command and direct all forces? Is this another meaningless expression? I mean, it doesn't say: There will be a combined command post, as you try to tell us it means. It would have been easy enough to say there will be a combined command post. So what on earth is the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, this is unfortunate wording. In reality a combined command post is from where the army forces were commanded down one chain and the MUP forces down another chain, an autonomous chain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us now have a look at the next document, that is, P1967. It says that this is an addendum to a document, obviously to a previous document. Did you have occasion to see this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an amendment to the decision of the Pristina Corps on supporting the MUP forces in breaking up and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the area of Malo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, first of all could you tell me whose decision can be amended?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In the process of decision-making, the right to amend a decision is exercised only by the commander himself. This is a correction. Because this is an open process, an open-ended process.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us now look at the last page of this document. We have seen here in the heading it also says "Joint Command." So please let us have a look at the last page, and it seems that here in the left-hand corner this amendment was designed by corps commander General Lazarevic. Can you explain this to us? Why do we now see this signature of the corps commander here, although the heading says "Joint Command" and although this is an amendment to a preceding decision where it says "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear that this is a telegram. In order for one like this to be dispatched and sent down the chain of command to subordinate commands to be carried out, it has to be signed. In this case, the corps commander signed this amendment to one of his own decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, do you remember this action that occurred in Malo Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there was a command post for this action; and if so, where it was?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the document, you see that the command post was in the Lausa sector. This was also the command post for the 354th Infantry Brigade. The corps commander set up a team for purposes of command and dispatched this team to the Lausa sector, which was the place from which the team led the operation in Malo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were you a part of that team also; if not, do you know who was there and why was this particular place so appropriate for setting up command there?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember each single person right now. Normally there would be three to five officers from the corps command. I know that Colonel Kokolanski, the officer in charge of training was there; as well as Colonel Nikolic, who was the chief of that particular branch. I can't remember right now who the others were, who were members of that team. Why right there? Because right above Lausa village there is Lausa hill, which has a very commanding position and is thus an appropriate place from which to run an action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have another document now, please, I think the format is the same as the previous one. This is an OTP Exhibit P2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you remember this document, sir, another one by the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order in relation to Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go to page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It talks about readiness for this action. The very last sentence in the B/C/S, if we could please pull it up just ever so slightly. General, you see readiness for this action, the 3rd of April, 1999, 7.00?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, please, let us move on to Defence Exhibit 5D84. This is a combat report by the Pristina Corps command dated the 3rd of April. It was sent to the 3rd Army command, specifically their operations centre. General, can you just, please, read item 2.1, activities, effects, consequences, and other. Slowly, please?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Activities, results, consequences, and other: "Pursuant to the decision of the Pristina Corps commander, the planning to regroup forces was brought to completion and operations are underway to seal off and crush Siptar terrorist forces in the general Jablanica sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this combat report in reference to the action mentioned in the previous document, where in the header it reads the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: All right. Can we now please move on to 5D85. This is another combat report of the Pristina Corps command. It was sent to the 3rd Army command. Item 2.1, please, if you could have a look. It also reads: "Activities, results, consequences, and other ..." Can you please read that one for us, too, slowly.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "The action aimed at crushing the Siptar terrorist forces in the wider Jablanica sector is underway and pursuant to the decision by the Pristina Corps commander it will be completed by nightfall on the 4th of April, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, is this combat report too in reference to the order that we looked at a while ago that reads in its header "the Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So why does this combat report reflect the same thing as the previous one, during the action in the Jablanica sector and pursuant to the decision by the Pristina Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Because the Jablanica order was issued by the corps commander as well, that's why, and we see him here reporting to submitting a report to his superior commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. Just before the break, if we could please look at another document, another order, which has the Joint Command in its header. This is OTP Exhibit P1969. General, if you look at the header you will see "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija" and the date is the 28th of March, 1998 [as interpreted]. Order on supporting MUP forces in routing and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the Malisevo sector. Are you familiar with this one, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So whose decision is this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The same as all the previous ones that we've been looking at. If you look at the format, you will see that, these are decisions by the Pristina Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D371, please, which is another combat report dated the 1st of April. The order is dated the 28th of March and the combat report is dated the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you please look at that, sir, and please read the sentence under 2.1 "activities, results, consequences, and other ..."

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Activities were continued on crushing and breaking up the Siptar terrorist forces in the Malisevo area in accordance with the general idea and decision by the commander of the Pristina Corps. The action will be completed in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this combat report also in reference to the previous order that we saw with the header that reads: "The Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this might be a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac. Thank you. Mr. Stefanovic, we have to break at this stage for 20 minutes. Could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And we shall resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, there are several orders like this. We'll be looking at another one. It's so to be Exhibit P1878. This order has the same format as the previous ones that I've been showing you, an order to crush and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the Rugovo sector. Do you remember this order, sir, and this particular action?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Page 2, item 4: "Decision and readiness." So the action is supposed to be launched at 6.00 on the 18th of April, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the section entitled: "Readiness" says, 6.00, 18th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at Exhibit 5D194. Your Honours, there was amendment to the translation of this document because this is something that was challenged earlier on in the trial, and the original translation was at one point amended by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this is a letter from the Pristina Corps command to the 3rd Army command, as far as I can see. Could you read paragraph 2 for us and comment briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "At 0800 hours on the 18th of April, 1999, the Pristina Corps command, in coordination with the forces of the Serbian MUP, shall launch an operation to break up and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the said sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what is this about? There's an action being announced here. And who will carry it out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The corps commander hereby informs the army commander of the fact that on this day and at this time the corps command will work in coordination with the MUP forces in order to launch an action to crush and destroy Siptar terrorist forces in the Rugovo area, the Rugovo cliffs area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we go to the last paragraph of this document and please explain this, there's a reference there to the Podgorica Corps. Was this corps part of the VJ at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Podgorica Corps was part of the VJ, part of the 2nd Army, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Since it was part of the 2nd Army and not the 3rd, was it necessary to organize coordination and communication with them as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: In this specific action it was necessary to make sure there was someone in charge from the Podgorica Corps who would be their neighbour for this action, in order to have coordinated action and in order to have the communications system fully operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So what is the specific assignment? If you look at paragraph 3 you might be able to see that. What was the task for units of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Pristina Corps forces shall block the Radovac hydro-electric power-plant - Bresotvik village - Markova Pecina line or axis."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. So the date on this is the 15th of April. We saw that order which says readiness on the 18th of April, and we see in this document that the action will be launched on the 18th of April. Now, please, can we go to the combat report dated the 19th of April, this is 5D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do, is this a normal document in the ordinary exchange of orders and combat reports or is this an exceptional document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this sort of document is always introduced in situations such as this one when there are several commands from several different operative or strategic units. For example, here we see the Podgorica Corps of the 2nd Army as our neighbour. It is necessary to go through the Supreme Command Staff, or rather, the General Staff in order to secure precisely what is being requested here, to make sure that there is someone over there, an officer in charge of setting up the communications system. This is a perfectly normal thing in situations such as this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that the only reason why this document has been written? If the Podgorica Corps was not involved, would this document have been written?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if the Podgorica Corps had had no assignment to carry out, if there had been no need for their involvement, well, there would have been no need to get in touch with them and to ask for their involvement; but they were our first neighbour. In this case it was necessary to ensure that there would be coordinated action and that a communications system would be in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not understanding this, Mr. Bakrac. I don't particularly have in my memory another example of this type of letter, and I'm trying to understand its relevance beyond making sure that there are good communication arrangements in place with the Podgorica Corps. But I'm -- the witness is leaving me in doubt about whether this would be written whether the Podgorica Corps were involved or not. As I say, I don't remember similar documents before the operation -- the actions were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, do you want me to explore this any further?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, I want to understand how frequently we -- these documents were produced, because it doesn't follow a formula that I'm in -- certainly my memory is familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, is this an example of a situation where a corps from the 2nd Army was involved? Is there any participation in other situations or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a specific task that is discussed here, and I can't recall any other situations where the involvement of another operative unit outside the 3rd Army was requested.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this not a reason then for the fact that we see to the 3rd Army command, Chief of Staff personally, why was it requested that someone from the Podgorica Corps should be put in charge of setting up the command system?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: It's just like I said, in order to make sure there was coordinated action, in order to make sure that a communications system was in place. You can't have a corps command addressing directly the Podgorica Corps for a request like that and to make sure that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So in paragraph 5 here we see that it was necessary to have the involvement of the Podgorica Corps to prevent spillover of Siptar terrorist forces into Montenegro. Were they involved in this action or in the blockade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is how it is defined here, that is precisely what coordinated action means, to block, to prevent spillover of Siptar terrorist forces into Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were the Podgorica Corps mentioned in the previous document, P1878, the actual order?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it might be a good idea for us to bring that document back. Your Honours, I think it's in paragraph 3, item 1 of paragraph 3. It says what the objective of the Siptar terrorist forces operations is, to overrun -- to secure the corridor from the Rugovo gorge to Montenegro and then we see exactly at item 3 "neighbours."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you read 3.2 and tell us what PGP means, what it stands for.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: 3.2, that stands for the Podgorica Corps, it is to set up a blockade along the Cakor-Hajla axis, the objective being to prevent spillover infiltration of Siptar terrorist forces from the Rugovo sector into Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English there is an error in the translation of this document. The abbreviation in the Serbian is PGK, which means the Podgorica Corps, it is not PrK which is the Pristina Corps. It is erroneously reflected in the English, where it reads the Pristina Corps, whereas it should read the Podgorica Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has a change not been made to the exhibit since this was discovered?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, I was talking about the previous document that we were looking at 194, 5D194, that's where the error was found and where it was rectified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In that case, you will need to file an alternative translation to this one to clarify the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, we shall do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, it shouldn't be necessary to go through the normal formality for this. If you can provide an English version on which paragraph 3.2 is altered and substitute it, with the assistance of the registrar, for the existing one, then we will authorise that replacement here and now and avoid the need for formal filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just to be clear on this, of course I do accept this obligation, but this is a Prosecution document so is it all right for me to do this? I don't mind doing it, but is it all right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. It should be Mr. Stamp that's doing it, and he'll do it, no doubt, on the same basis as we have just explained, to avoid unnecessary filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, if I understood you correctly, this is the only example of participation by the Pristina -- by the Podgorica Corps, and that is why it was included in the document?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now, can the commander of the Pristina Corps issue an order to the commander of the Podgorica Corps?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: He cannot. Obviously he cannot. It's the same level from different armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is that the reason why the Podgorica Corps is referred to under the heading "Neighbours"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, that's what I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to move on to the next document, if we have explored this sufficiently, as you asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I still don't know the answer to the question whether 5D194 is a routine document or is one which is only required where there's a neighbour to whom the Pristina Corps cannot issue instructions. That's all I want to know. And the witness wasn't apparently able to explain that, so I wondered if there is any further questioning you can conduct that will help; if not, move on to something else and perhaps it will become clearer later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am going to put a question now, as you've suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this an exceptional document because the commander of the Pristina Corps could not issue orders to the commander of the Podgorica Corps, document 5D194, the one that we've been looking at?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. President, I have understood what it was that you were asking for. This is a unique occasion when the command of the Podgorica Corps was being addressed. However, in the procedure and in view of the circumstances involved, this is customary form in order to ensure the involvement of a neighbour in carrying out a task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5D1411, could we please have that called up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this is a combat report of the command of the Pristina Corps dated the 19th of April. We have seen that a particular action was being planned for the 18th of April. Could you please look at paragraph 2.1: "Activities, impact, consequences, and other," and could you please read paragraph number 2 to us, that is to say actions that started.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: "Actions that started in searching the terrain in the areas of Rugovo gorge, Zlas, and Drenica are also evolving according to plan. Units of the Pristina Corps are involved in the blockade of the sector and the MUP units, the units of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia are involved in searching the terrain."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: This combat report on the engagement of the units of the Pristina Corps, do they have to do with the previous order that says "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What would be interesting, Mr. Bakrac, in light of the answer to the previous question about 5D194 would be to see similar examples where there was this additional exchange of communication to clarify the position of the MUP in a Joint Command action.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are precisely going to get to that subject now. I have another document or two and we will be discussing this relationship between the units of the Pristina Corps and the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us now please look at 5D373, it's a very short document and it's a document of the command of the Pristina Corps. I would just be interested in hearing your brief comments on this document. General, are you familiar with this document and what does it relate to?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document relates to the request, or rather, where the corps command is asking for effects of breaking the Siptar terrorist forces. So an analysis is being requested by 1400 hours on the 25th of April, and it has to do with several actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are these predominantly actions that pertain to the orders that have the heading "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Tell us, please, do you remember how many orders there were like this in total with the heading of "Joint Command," in 1999, that is, and until when was this format, or rather, this form used?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: There were about 20 such orders -- or to be more specific, between 15 and 20, and this went on until the order was issued on the resubordination of the MUP to the army. Order of the command of the 3rd Army, and before that, of the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Approximately what date was this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: It's about the 18th or 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in addition to these joint actions of the VJ and the MUP and the actions in support of forces, did the units of the Pristina Corps have independent combat as well; and if so, to what extent?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Every day there was combat, throughout the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in all zones of the units that were subordinated to the brigade command, not only taking into account external attacks from the border. There were several hundred combats of this nature, over 500 throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. You told us earlier on that the focus of the activity, or rather, the focus of the task of the Pristina Corps was to defend part of the territory of the FRY, or rather, of Kosovo and Metohija. What did the command of the Pristina Corps do with regard to this question once the war started?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The corps command at the beginning of the war issued several orders to take urgent measures, with a view to planning, organizing, and preparing to carry out a persistent defence of the state border engaging the main forces of the corps and with a lesser degree of the forces they were to support and coordinate action with the MUP forces in crushing the terrorist forces in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, can we now have a look at 5D312. It seems that this is an order of the commander -- of the command of the Pristina Corps from the very beginning, from the first day of the war, the 25th of March, 1999. Are you familiar with this order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us please look at page 2, paragraph 6, and can you give us your comments briefly, what this order implied.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 orders as follows: "By the 27th of March, 1999, ensure that precise and clear commands are issued at all command levels for the execution of ultimate persistent defence of the very -- from the very state border."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have a look at 5D -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Rather, let us first hear from you on this. Did the brigade commands indeed make plans for defence and did they issue orders for defending the country?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All brigades in the corps started carrying out this task issued by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us please look at 5D335 now. That is also an order of the commander of the Pristina Corps, but this one is dated the 26th of March. The previous one was the 25th of March. Please look at paragraph 1 of this order and give us your brief comments.

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Article 1: "Continue with the decisive defence of the state border, prevent any surprises in the form of infiltration of the Siptar terrorist forces from the Republic of Albania and the Republic of Macedonia" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please don't read. If you can just look at the three last axes, Globocanica, Doganovici, and so on, and then we will look at the next document and you can say whether this order was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now can we look at document 5D1284.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, the document will appear soon. This is a defence order of the 26th of March of the 243rd Motorised Brigade. Under the heading: "Tasks or assignments" we see the three axes mentioned by the corps commander as needing to be secured. Is that the order that was implemented?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is an order of the command of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, did the Pristina Corps command adopt a defence order, defence order at the level of the corps command?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 5D175. Is that the order, do you recognise it, and did you take part in the drafting of the same?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order by the Pristina Corps command drafted on the 6th of April and, yes, I was one of the bearers of this act, this command -- this order.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you briefly comment about whether this order is precisely the main activity that you talked about or focuses on the main activity?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order for the main and basic assignment of the Pristina Corps, and that is the defence of the state border and a part of the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said earlier, General, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's a matter of clarification. Perhaps the date -- the date of the document could be clarified. I think there might be a mistake in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, the original shows 1999, so we'll assume a mistake in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, in English I see that it says "1998." It's evidently a typo because we're talking about the 6th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, sir, earlier you said how long the orders were issued with the heading "Joint Command." You said that this was until the order on resubordination was issued, and did this resubordination actually take place of the MUP units to the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: No. After the Pristina Corps issued its resubordination command in relation to the MUP, this resubordination never took place throughout the war until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know why this resubordination was not carried out and do you know if there was an attempt to actually implement this resubordination?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The corps command attempted several times to resolve this question with the MUP members, the question of resubordination, and the corps command, or rather, the corps commander formed a number of teams from the command to make an effort to resolve this resubordination matter in the field. All of those efforts did not yield any results. The most frequent response from the MUP members was that they do not have an order from their superiors to execute this assignment, the resubordination to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So at which level was this relationship of the Army of Yugoslavia with MUP throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The functional relationship between the army and the MUP was at the level that it was before the resubordination order was issued, at the level of coordinated action, joint action, support, and cooperation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, thank you. Could you please explain to us how this coordination and cooperation proceeded?

utterances.speaker: RADOJKO STEFANOVIC
utterances.text: The coordination with the organs or the representatives of the MUP most often was effected in the following way, by going or calling the MUP representatives tasked with planning, and it boiled down to exchange of data and information in order to coordinate joint actions. After that, when an agreement was reached, each side would go to their respective command and convey in the depth what was agreed on at this operations level.
